project: Library loans: books, members, loans, fines.
canonicalSource: Martin, R. C. (2017). Clean Architecture: A Craftsman's Guide to Software Structure and Design. Prentice Hall. Ch. 22 (The Clean Architecture: the Dependency Rule), ch. 11 (DIP), ch. 14 (ADP), ch. 26 (The Main Component).
styleDefinition: Source-code dependencies point inward only: infrastructure -> application -> domain (the Dependency Rule).
The domain (entities, value objects, domain services, repository interfaces) depends on nothing outside itself and on no framework.
Use cases depend on abstractions (repository interfaces in the domain, ports such as Clock in the application), never on infrastructure classes.
Infrastructure implements the inner interfaces (repositories, gateways); controllers call use cases and exchange DTOs, not entities.
Main (the composition root) is the only module that knows every concrete class; it lives in the outermost circle.

notApplicable.reason: no-layer-skip applies to style layered only (template applicability)

outOfScope: Coupling metrics (FF-C*), SOLID proxies (FF-SO*), naming and convention rules (FF-CV*) and the neuronal functions (FF-N*) are not compared: they are threshold proxies or conventions (FR-V6 makes them advisory), and they say nothing about whether a planted architectural violation is caught. The runner lists their rows separately as unscored.
